summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, alcohol dependence, dementia, and chronic aspiration was admitted for acute respiratory failure and septic shock due to aspiration pneumonia. He required ICU care, vasopressor support, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. A central line was placed initially, later replaced with a PICC line. He was treated for concurrent COPD exacerbation and mild heart failure with steroids and diuretics. Hyponatremia was managed with fluid restriction. Goals of care were discussed, confirming the patient's DNR/DNI status and refusal of a feeding tube despite high aspiration risk. He improved clinically, was stabilized on oxygen, and transitioned to extended care with plans to complete IV antibiotics and outpatient follow-up for pulmonary and swallowing issues.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit
Syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with (acute) exacerbation
